content.title: Oscars 2026: KPop Demon Hunters’ Golden wins Best Original Song; speech cut off sparks backlash
content.text: KPop Demon Hunters’ Golden wins Best Original Song Oscar; acceptance speech cut off, sparks reactions onlineThe song ‘Golden’ from the animated film KPop Demon Hunters won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, becoming the first K-pop track to take home the Oscar at the 98th Academy Awards.The track was written by EJAE, Mark Sonnenblick, Joong Gyu Kwak, Yu-Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Jeong Hoon Seo and Teddy Park. It marked the first Oscar nomination and win for all seven contributors. The win also meant that EJAE, Ido and Teddy Park became the first South Koreans to win in the Best Original Song category. During the ceremony, EJAE delivered an emotional acceptance speech and reflected on her journey. “People made fun of me for liking K-pop,” she said, adding that she was proud that “everyone’s singing our song and all the Korean lyrics.”She described the award as a moment of perseverance rather than achievement. “This award is not about success, it's about resilience,” EJAE said while accepting the honour.However, the moment was cut short when collaborator Yu-Han Lee began reading his speech. The orchestra music started playing almost immediately, signalling the team to wrap up, and the camera pulled away as the broadcast moved to a commercial break.Social media reactionsThe interruption sparked criticism online, with several viewers calling the decision disrespectful and questioning why the team was cut off so quickly. Some social media users also pointed out that members of the KPop Demon Hunters team appeared to be cut short earlier in the evening as well.The interruption triggered strong reactions online, with several viewers calling the move disrespectful.“I’m sorry but this was so disrespectful to cut KPop Demon Hunters speech… #Oscars,” wrote one user.Another commented, “Golden winning a #Oscar but then getting cut off hard at the acceptance speech was racist.”A third user wrote, “Well deserved Oscar for Best Original Song, but a shame the Academy cut them short and did not allow them finishing their gracious acceptance speech, but allowing other Oscar winners to go over time.”“This felt sad and disrespectful! When all other category winners were given time for their acceptance speech, why was it cut when Kpop Demon Hunters Original Song Winners were still giving speech?” another user said.“My brain would torment me forever if I got an Oscar and was cut off from saying my speech. No one deserves that,” another post read.‘Golden’ beat other nominees including ‘Dear Me’ from Diane Warren: Relentless, ‘I Lied to You’ from Sinners, ‘Sweet Dreams of Joy’ from Viva Verdi! and ‘Train Dreams’ from Train Dreams. The award was also the second Oscar of the evening for KPop Demon Hunters, which earlier won Best Animated Feature.Relaxo Footwears elevates Gaurav Dua, Ritesh Dua as Co-CEOsRelaxo Footwears Ltd names Gaurav Kumaar Dua and Ritesh Dua Co Chief Executive Officers from April 1 2026 marking a shift to a dual shared leadership model.By Storyboard18| March 27, 2026, 00:01:27 ISTRelaxo Footwears reshuffles leadership, creates Co-CEO rolesRelaxo Footwears Ltd has announced a leadership reshuffle, elevating senior executives Gaurav Kumaar Dua and Ritesh Dua to Co-Chief Executive Officers, as the company moves towards a dual leadership structure.Gaurav Kumaar Dua, currently Whole-time Director, has been re-designated as Co-Chief Executive Officer and Whole-time Director (Co-CEO & WTD), while Ritesh Dua, Executive Vice President (Finance), will take on the role of Co-Chief Executive Officer. Both appointments will take effect from April 1, 2026.The company said the redesignations will be on existing remuneration, with no change in tenure or other terms approved by shareholders at the annual general meeting held on August 24, 2023. Their current tenure runs from October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2026.The appointments signal a transition towards a shared leadership model at the footwear major, with responsibilities expected to be split across business operations and strategic functions.Gaurav Dua brings over 25 years of experience in sales and marketing within the footwear industry. An MBA from the University of Wales, he has led several initiatives across revenue growth, market expansion and brand development at Relaxo. He is also part of the promoter family and the son of Managing Director Ramesh Kumar Dua.Ritesh Dua, who has more than 26 years of experience, has overseen key functions including finance, human resources, information technology and exports. An MBA from the Fore School of Management, Delhi, he has played a central role in strengthening the company’s operational backbone. He is part of the promoter group and related to senior leadership, including Whole-time Director Nikhil Dua.From Kiran Mani to Irina Ghose: Indian-origin leaders in key roles across global AI firmsOpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft have hired leaders like Kiran Mani, Arvind KC and Rahul Patil, as Indian-origin executives take on key roles across AI expansion, infrastructure and policy. By Storyboard18| March 26, 2026, 23:46:01 ISTFrom OpenAI to Anthropic, Indian-origin leaders take key roles The global AI race is increasingly being shaped by who companies are hiring, and a growing number of those leaders are Indian or Indian-origin executives stepping into critical roles across OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI firms.From policy and partnerships to engineering and people operations, these hires show how AI companies are building leadership depth beyond research. India, in particular, is emerging as both a talent hub and a strategic market, with firms actively hiring senior leaders to drive expansion, regulation, and adoption.Kiran Mani joins OpenAI as APAC Managing DirectorOpenAI appointed Kiran Mani, former CEO of JioStar, as Managing Director for Asia-Pacific. He will relocate to Singapore and take charge in June, reporting to Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon. The role has been created as OpenAI looks to expand its enterprise and consumer footprint across Asia-Pacific, including India.Asha Sharma leads Microsoft’s AI-first gaming push Asha Sharma was appointed Executive Vice President at Microsoft, where she leads Microsoft Gaming and the Xbox ecosystem, including the integration of Activision Blizzard, with an AI-first approach. She had rejoined Microsoft in 2024 to work on Core AI initiatives before moving into the gaming leadership role.Arvind KC joins OpenAI as Chief People Officer Arvind KC was appointed Chief People Officer at OpenAI, where he now leads hiring, onboarding, and organisational systems as the company rapidly scales its workforce. He brings prior experience from leadership roles at Roblox, Google and Workday, combining engineering and people operations expertise. Rahul Patil joins Anthropic as Chief Technology Officer Rahul Patil joined Anthropic as Chief Technology Officer, where he oversees engineering, infrastructure, and security, bringing experience from roles at Stripe, AWS, and Microsoft. He succeeded cofounder Sam McCandlish in the role as Anthropic scales its technical capabilities. Sachin Katti heads compute infrastructure at OpenAI Sachin Katti joined OpenAI to lead compute infrastructure, focusing on scaling hardware systems and custom silicon needed for advanced AI models and AGI ambitions. He previously served as Chief Technology and AI Officer at Intel and has also been a Stanford professor and startup founder. Irina Ghose leads Anthropic India expansion Anthropic appointed Irina Ghose, former Managing Director of Microsoft India, to lead its India operations. Her appointment comes as the company expands its footprint in the country, including opening a Bengaluru office, positioning India as a key market for its Claude AI models. Her role is focused on building local teams and driving enterprise adoption of Anthropic’s AI offerings in India.Pragya Mishra leads OpenAI for government relations in India As part of its early India push, OpenAI hired Pragya Mishra as its first government relations lead in the country in 2024. The move laid the groundwork for regulatory engagement and policy alignment as the company scaled its presence in India. Her role centres on policy outreach, partnerships and stakeholder engagement in one of OpenAI’s fastest-growing markets.From IIT to Silicon Valley: 5 Indian-origin leaders making it big in the USTheir journeys from India’s top engineering institutions to global leadership roles highlight the growing influence of Indian-origin professionals in international markets.By Storyboard18| March 26, 2026, 23:07:58 ISTSeveral IIT alumni have gone on to lead some of the world’s most influential companies, shaping innovation, enterprise strategy and the future of technology.[caption id="attachment_93359" align="alignnone" width="1280"] Sundar Pichai currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of Alphabet Inc. and Google, making him one of the most influential figures in the global technology industry.Born in Madurai, Pichai completed his B.Tech in metallurgical engineering from IIT Kharagpur, graduating in 1993. Reports stated that his professors described him as shy, quiet and exceptionally intelligent during his time at the institute.[/caption][caption id="attachment_93360" align="alignnone" width="1280"] Arvind Krishna is the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of IBM and is another IIT alumnus who has made a significant mark in global business. He earned a degree in electrical engineering from IIT Kanpur, graduating in 1985. He later moved to the United States to pursue a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.[/caption][caption id="attachment_93361" align="alignnone" width="1280"] Vinod Khosla is an American billionaire businessman and venture capitalist, best known as the co-founder of Sun Microsystems.Khosla completed his bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from IIT Delhi, where he studied between 1971 and 1976. He later moved to the United States to continue his education at Carnegie Mellon University.[/caption][caption id="attachment_93362" align="alignnone" width="1280"] Aravind Srinivas is the co-founder and CEO of Perplexity AI.Born in Chennai, he graduated from IIT Madras in 2017 with a dual degree in electrical engineering. He went on to earn a PhD in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley and held research roles at organisations such as OpenAI, Google Brain and DeepMind before launching Perplexity in 2022.[/caption][caption id="attachment_93364" align="alignnone" width="1280"] Nikesh Arora has served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Palo Alto Networks since 2018.He graduated in 1989 from the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi. Prior to his current role, Arora held leadership positions at SoftBank Group as President and Chief Business Officer, and also worked as a senior executive at Google.[/caption]
